description:
PROBLEM. When a benchmark cannot load because an import fails, users get no actionable instruction: MCP returns "Benchmark '<name>' requires additional dependencies" (benchbox/mcp/tools/benchmark.py:559,810; benchbox/mcp/jobs.py:1151) and the CLI says "Benchmark 'tpcdi' not supported yet. Available: ...tpcdi..." (benchbox/cli/benchmark_loader.py:121-125). Root cause: `get_public_benchmark_class` (benchbox/core/benchmark_registry.py:276-285) converts ImportError, AttributeError and a missing class into None, discarding the missing module. In addition `_BENCHMARK_REGISTRY.optional_dependencies` (benchbox/__init__.py:60-73) lists extras that do not exist in pyproject (ssb, amplab, h2odb, clickbench, joinorder, coffeeshop; only `tpcdi` exists), and `create_import_error` (benchbox/utils/version.py:457-470) prints them as install advice.

CHANGE. (1) The lookup surfaces the import failure: a ModuleNotFoundError/ImportError is reported with the missing module name (`ModuleNotFoundError.name`); AttributeError or a missing class is an internal error, not a missing dependency. (2) Correct `optional_dependencies` to extras that exist in pyproject. (3) One message source used by MCP (reusing the existing `MCPError.suggestion` field and the DEPENDENCY_MISSING code; no new envelope fields), the CLI loader and the Python API: names the module, the extra when one maps, and the install command from `get_install_command` (benchbox/utils/dependencies.py:43); without a mapped extra, names the module and points to https://benchbox.dev/docs/ installation guide page that exists. (4) changelog.d fragment (fix).
